x: Here we had Don Brown, fresh from his win in the Surrey County Championship, and Percy Wright, opposed by Hancock and Amer, of S.W.C. Our chance had gone, but our rivalry still continued, and there was still second place in the competition to be consolidated.
Meanwhile, Percy Wright, of our D team, was doing splendidly and with 19th position and 7 mins. 10 secs allowance, claimed the first handicap prize.
Jack Bidgood was 8th, Wright 10th, Saunders 14th, and Frank Elson 19th. Chief recollections are of terrible conditions, and of some fine walking by Churcher in spite of the fogginess.
The last event of the programme was the one mile, and with a lead on points, and Don Brown to represent us here, and Wright to back him up, we expected to win the competition.

We shall recall the Indolence that was Rollins' the Intrepidity that was Ring (he's had his teeth drawn now, though!), the Inscrutability that was Scrimshaw, the Immensity that was Ben May, and Illogicality that was Wright!

Pope, Fletcher and Wright preferred to start comparatively slowly, and speed up as the race progressed. Churcher walked strongly throughout and dropping his opponents, won fairly easily from Bidgood and Bentley, who were to fight out the Police Long Distance Championship on the following Thursday.

Captain Charlie Churcher finished in fourth position, and Percy Wright was fifth. Actually there is no scratch team race in this particular event (only a set of prizes for fastest team not gaining handicap awards) or Percy would have found himself in the unique position of finishing fifth in an open…
Wright of the "Poly." fourth.
100 Yds.—1, Broadbent (S.); 2, Bowers (S.); 3, Wright (N.).
Wright taking fourth place, and in the first of the 220 Yards races Bowers finished second to Wigley of the Triangle, but in the second race Wright won, beating Littler of the home club.

At seven miles Proctor was well away in the lead, Charlie and Mac still 5th and 6th, Readman 12th, Oliver 18th, Sapcote 20th, Bidgood 24th, Bentley 26th, Wright 28th, with Clayton taking it easy owing to a strained leg.

…rlie Churcher and Pat Sapcote, with Bob McMullen, walking his first 20, some 40 yards further back, followed by Messrs. Wright, Bidgood, Bentley and Oliver. It is interesting to note that Jack Rutland, who finished 4th, was at this stage 12th.…

A team of four supported the South Wales Argus 15½ miles Open promoted by Newport Harriers, and the race provided an opportunity for Messrs. Wright, Rutland and Robbins for a reunion with friends and relatives. There was a good entry with 42 individuals and 4 teams.

Then came Percy Wright, walking perhaps faster than anybody, and our hopes were right back again. This state of affairs caused much blood pressure, but Woodford managed to hold on to their slender lead.
Wright, came in third just in front of Brian Trower. Wright easily won the sealed handicap held in conjunction with G.

At the start Bert Clayton and Percy Wright got away fairly quickly and at two miles led by about 50 yards. Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakel…
Boreham, while the two back-markers, Maclean and Wright, filled the other placed positions.

In the Youths' event our lads got away to a good start with Wright and Goode up in the first half-dozen. Then came tragedy in the fact that they were wrongly directed and by the time they got back on the right course they had lost quite a lot of ground and places.
Henn, our Oxford University member, in second place and Frank Wright really showed the locals some running by "walking" the junior race over this distance.
Frank Wright was third in the individual race and it was interesting to note that we had our six counters home before any of the other teams, but our lads packed a little too far back.
Walker put in a really fine run to put them in the lead on the 3rd stage, and this was maintained by Wright, Short, Lucas and Bedford down to the end of the 7th relay.
